title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 48-50 of the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes). Grothendieck is studying lattices Fig(L) of 'figures' in a space L, together with the maps between them induced by a map of spaces: inverse images f^* and phi^*, direct images phi_* and i_* along inclusions, and products F -> F x F'. On the previous page he records that f^*, phi^* and phi_* commute with arbitrary Sups, that phi_* commutes with Infs of nonempty families, and that inclusions satisfy i^* i_* = id and a projection formula. On this page (numbered 49 in the manuscript) the elements X, Y of these lattices are viewed as 'multiplicités'. He compares them by several relations: X <= Y, X << Y, a ringed variant (X ring-<< Y), and a symmetric relation X |o| Y. These seem to be relations of relative size or dimension, not plain inclusion. This is an inference from context: plain inclusion is always preserved by preimages, yet he says <= is not. Page 50 confirms the picture: under f^* a multiplicity is sent 'to an iso' if f is surjective, and 'to an iso or to the empty set' in general.

The claim on this page: for the explicit inverse image f^* along a non-surjective f, with X' = f^*X and Y' = f^*Y:
- X ring-<< Y implies X' ring-<< Y';
- but neither X <= Y implies X' <= Y', nor even X << Y implies X' << Y'.
The reason: Y can lie outside the image of f, so Y' = empty, while X meets the image, so X' is nonempty.

His conclusion: such inverse images, which are not 'embeddings' and involve a 'passage to the quotient', must be handled with great care. They do not qualify as 'morphisms of ateliers' (his name for these structured lattices of figures with their size relations). A genuine morphism of ateliers would preserve ring-<<, <= and hence <<. Even so, in every case f^* preserves |o|.

The next page names the delicate point: passing to the quotient takes us out of the 'homéomorphisme passe-partout' setting. It then gives Example 2, the map F |-> F x F' = pr_1^*F . pr_2^*F'.

The problem served is axiomatizing the functoriality of a 'tame topology' or dimension-theoretic structure (an 'atelier'): deciding which operations between lattices of figures count as morphisms.
errors: No mathematical error. The counterexample (Y outside the image of f, X meeting it) correctly shows that a size/multiplicity preorder is not preserved by preimage along a non-surjective map.

Uncertainty: the exact meanings of <=, <<, ring-<< and |o| are defined on pages not given here. My reading as dimension or size comparisons rather than inclusion is an inference. The claim that |o| is preserved 'in all cases' depends on its definition and cannot be checked from this page alone.

ideas.what: Preimage along a non-surjective map does not preserve a 'size/multiplicity' preorder on figures, because parts outside the image collapse to the empty set. Only some relations (ring-<<, |o|) survive.
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality and monotonicity of dimension-type invariants under definable maps (cf. o-minimal / tame geometry)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; o-minimal dimension theory (van den Dries, Knight-Pillay-Steinhorn, 1980s-90s)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is only programmatically sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); 'ateliers' are not in published texts as far as I know

ideas.what: Defining 'morphisms of ateliers' as maps of figure-lattices preserving the order relations <=, << and ring-<<. Preimages that involve a quotient (non-embeddings) are excluded.
ideas.modern_name: Morphisms of structured lattices of definable sets / of tame-topology structures

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'atelier' framework for analysis situs (tame topology) includes a notion of morphism that must preserve size relations among figures. He identifies non-surjective preimages, and quotients generally, as the obstruction. This axiomatic thread is not developed in the literature under his name.
missed.quote: Elles ne sont pas justiciables d'une notion de "morphismes" d'ateliers, si on en avait X ≤ Y ⇒ X' ≤ Y' donc aussi X ≪ Y ⇒ X' ≪ Y'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of modest historical interest for reconstructing Grothendieck's tame topology program alongside o-minimality. Mathematically it is an elementary observation.

deep.surprise_reason: An elementary but historically informative observation: it shows how Grothendieck was axiomatizing morphisms of 'ateliers' in his unpublished tame-topology program. No deep new result.
transcription_corrections: Page number at top is '49', not '89'.
Opening likely reads 'Il y a une difficulté avec f^*, et qui ne se présentent pas pour φ_*, i_*)' rather than 'X, Y [?] [?] difficultés'.
'avec {+grande+} [-précaution-] [?] attention' likely reads 'avec grande attention' ('attention' replaced over a struck word).
'si on en [?] ... vait' is the hyphenated 'si on en avait'.
Line 'de pourtant [?] de "morphismes"' is likely 'pour un/au bout de "morphismes" d'ateliers' (uncertain).
